newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak BSE to launch country's first bond index.
newsitem.headline: Slovak BSE to launch country's first bond index.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Monday it would launch the country's first bond index, the SDX, on October 1, in an attempt to improve market transparency.

The index will be calculated as a yield index, to reflect more cumulative yields over prices, given the current lack of market lquidity which can easily distort prices, Olga Dlugopolska of the BSE trading division told Reuters.
"We recorded relatively large number of new bond issues during the first half of this year, which made the market more attractive, but also less transparent," she said.
"We want to offer investors the chance to receive the figures on development of the index portfolio, rather than to watch the price movements in every issue," she added.
The SDX index will consist of two branches, one for the 12 state bond issues, and the second for the remainder of the some 80 issues registered in the market.
The index will reflect trading with bonds on the bourse floor, excluding direct trades. The starting level of both items was set at 100 points, Dlugopolska said.
Some 66,000 bonds were traded on the BSE floor, including all the state and non-state issues, on turnover of 906.7 million crowns in August. Average daily figures were not immediately available.
Analysts said that while an index was needed to measure the market, they doubted it would help cure its biggest problems, a lack of liquidity and low yields.
"At the moment, only the banks play seriously on this market as the corporate investors find the yields unattractive when you consider the value-added tax," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
"Then the corporate issuer often buys complete issue itself, to use it for repayment of its credits in the bank," he added.
